review.tagline: Python library and CLI that converts PDFs, Office files and more into structured text
review.summary: Docling parses PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, EPUB, images, audio and other formats into a unified DoclingDocument, with PDF layout, reading order, table structure, code and formula recognition. It exports to Markdown, HTML, DocLang, DocTags and lossless JSON. It runs locally via a CLI or Python API, with OCR, VLM support (GraniteDocling), an MCP server and a docling-serve API server.
review.audience: Developers preparing documents for RAG and LLM pipelines
strengths: Wide input coverage: PDF, Office, ODF, EPUB, email, Apple iWork, XBRL, audio, video
Local execution suits sensitive data and air-gapped environments
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, Crew AI and Haystack
Ships a CLI, Python API, MCP server and docling-serve HTTP server
weaknesses: Hardware requirements (RAM, GPU) are not stated in the README
Individual models carry their own licenses, separate from the MIT codebase
Metadata extraction and chemistry understanding are listed as coming soon
Requires Python 3.10 or higher; 3.9 support was dropped in 2.70.0
needs: Models: GraniteDocling, VLMs, OCR engines, ASR models
